title: Review of c37's lone-cell negative: on fresh seed 6 at mu=2, none of three transplanted median cells swims alone (net 1.02, 0.13 and 0.06 diameters before dying or splitting within 25-50 t); their in-place twins also stay below 1 diameter
summary: Ran c37's isolate_p.py unchanged on the C:swim-divide kernel world (20261026T0227-c29-kernel-ring-screen/world.py, drive kernel, mu 1, kd 0.08, chi 5) on unused seed 6: grown from noise to t=2400 (99 cells, median area 64 px), then the 3 median cells copied alone into a fresh S=1 bath with mu=2 and vmax=1.0 (ISO_P, EVERY=5), each against the same cell left in place. Isolated: cell 55 grows 65x and is lost at t+50 after 1.02 diameters; cells 43 and 54 split at t+30 and t+25 after 0.13 and 0.06 (they were about to divide when transplanted). In place: 0.95, 0.19 and 0.09. None reaches 3 diameters, as the finding reports for seed 5 (max 1.77 at mu=2). labkit re-run of the world on seed 6 (rerun/seed6): 215 persistent splits, generation 6, 114 tracks moving >= 1 body length (max 3.5).

observations.M: lone6_mu2.json: isolated cells net 1.02, 0.13, 0.06 diameters at mu=2 (seed 6); rerun/seed6/sheet.png shows the crowded colony the cells came from

seeds_run.result: pass: no lone cell reaches 3 diameters at mu=2

controls_run.M: in-place arm of isolate_p.py (same cells left in the colony at mu=2)

verdicts.limitation: Only mu=2 and one seed; two of my three median cells were dividing at transplant and split within 30 t, so they test little about swimming; the informative cell grew 65x in the fresh bath before it was lost, matching c37's 'growth outruns motion'. isolate_p.py wrote no snapshot figure for these short follow-ups.
